summary: Fixed O-045 only. `parsePort` now declares -port with `fs.Func` and parses the value as text through a new `decimal` helper: ASCII digits only, then `strconv.Atoi`. `010` reads as decimal 10, and `0x1F90`, `0o17`, `0b1`, `1_000`, `+80`, `-1` and Arabic-Indic digits are refused. The 1..65535 range check and the usage-on-refusal behaviour are unchanged. The review's test is at internal/testutil/seeded/port_decimal_test.go as given and passes. I added the base-prefix, underscore and sign rows to TestPortFlagRefusesBadValues, plus `010` and `08080` as decimal-accepted rows. No other file changed in this attempt.

files.why: -port is read as text via fs.Func and parsed as decimal (new decimal helper), instead of fs.Int's base-0 ParseInt
the code review's TestPortFlagReadsADecimalPort, as given
TestPortFlagRefusesBadValues gains rows for 0x1F90, 0o17, 0b1, 1_000, +80 and an Arabic-Indic number, and accepted rows 010 (10) and 08080 (8080)

obligations.how: In main.go, parsePort declares -port with fs.Func and reads the text through decimal(): ASCII digits only, then strconv.Atoi, so 010 is 10 and 0x1F90, 0o17, 0b1, 1_000, +80, -1 and a non-ASCII digit string are refused through flag's own error plus usage. The range check and the usage-on-refusal path are unchanged. `go test -count=1 -run ^TestPortFlagReadsADecimalPort$ ./internal/testutil/seeded` passes. With fs.Int restored in a scratch overlay it fails: 010 gives 8, 0x1F90 gives 8080, 0o17 gives 15, 0b1 gives 1, 1_000 gives 1000. The whole seeded package passes and gofmt and vet are clean. `go run ./internal/testutil/seeded -port 0x1F90` prints 'is not a decimal number' with the usage and does not start the product.

tests.note: with the new base-prefix, underscore and sign rows
expected failure: with fs.Int back, 010 gives 8, 0x1F90 8080, 0o17 15, 0b1 1, 1_000 1000

tests.command: go test -count=1 ./internal/testutil/seeded; go vet ./internal/testutil/seeded; gofmt -l on LF copies
tests.note: whole package passes; vet and gofmt clean
refused with 'is not a decimal number' and the usage; nothing started, no temp folders left

deviations: The review's wording said 'refusing a value that is not all decimal digits'. A leading zero is all digits, so 010 is read as decimal 10 and accepted, not refused; the review's own test allows either (an error, or 10).
not_built: O-044, O-046 and O-047 were waived by the review and are not built. IN-m3 was overridden. The ZZ_PROBE_DIR fallback in the probe source, the exec-pattern holes (a literal inside one nested call, python3.14t, pypy3) and the case-sensitive ls-files pathspecs stay as they were.
